surprises.body: Montréal’s shots at 5-on-5 had a 10.0% chance of scoring on the average shot, against their usual 6.5% and a league average of 6.4%. A team strays this far about once every 90 games.

story.head: Caufield has two goals as the Canadiens take down the Stars
paras: It was a busy first period. Cole Caufield got the scoring started for the Canadiens early in the period, but Wyatt Johnston made it 1-1 for Dallas on the power play midway through the period. Alex Newhook and Caufield scored 27 seconds apart late in the period to put the Habs up 3-1. Newhook struck again early in the second to make it 4-1, but Jamie Benn cut Montréal’s lead to 4-2 less than three minutes later. Phillip Danault added an empty-net goal with 48 seconds left to make it 5-2.

The Canadiens had the better of the chances. Jakub Dobeš made 17 saves for the Canadiens, and Jake Oettinger stopped 16 of 20 at the other end. The Canadiens improved to 8-3-2, second in the Atlantic, while the Stars dropped to 7-5-1, slipping to fourth in the Central.

items.text: Four straight wins for the Canadiens.
Chris Kreider extended his point streak against Dallas to seven games.
With Nick Suzuki out, Newhook took his spot and scored twice, though he won only 4 of 15 faceoffs.
The Stars’ Trey Taylor played his first NHL game.
